About The Job Opportunity

The Data Analyst supports PartsSource's growth and operational excellence by transforming raw data into actionable insights. Working with business stakeholders across sales, operations, product, and finance, you will conduct detailed analyses on customer behavior, operational metrics, and business opportunities—identifying patterns, trends, and optimization opportunities. This role combines technical data skills with business acumen to answer complex questions, support strategic decisions, and uncover new value creation opportunities. You'll develop repeatable analytical processes, document findings clearly for diverse audiences, and stay curious about how emerging tools—including AI—can enhance analytical quality and efficiency.

What You'll Do

Data Preparation & Analysis

Extract, clean, and organize data from multiple sources to prepare datasets for analysis.
Conduct detailed quantitative analyses to identify patterns, trends, and insights that address specific business questions.
Use SQL to query databases and retrieve data; apply Excel and visualization tools to explore and communicate findings.
Validate analytical work for accuracy and completeness; document methodologies and assumptions clearly.

Reporting & Communication

Develop clear, compelling reports and dashboards that translate complex findings into actionable recommendations for business stakeholders.
Prepare written summaries of analytical findings with clear explanations of methodology, assumptions, and business implications.
Present analyses and recommendations to cross-functional teams and leadership, tailoring communication to audience and context.
Collaborate with stakeholders to understand analytical needs and define scope for data projects.

Process Improvement & Tool Development

Identify opportunities to streamline analytical workflows and reduce manual work through better processes or automation.
Create and document repeatable analysis templates, queries, and workflows that enable consistent output and knowledge sharing across the team.
Stay current with emerging analytical tools and methodologies, including practical applications of AI; experiment with new approaches to enhance efficiency and insight quality.
Support team members in understanding analytical methodologies and best practices.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Work with sales, operations, product, and finance teams to understand their analytical needs and deliver insights that support business decisions.
Translate between technical analytical concepts and business language to ensure clarity and alignment.
Contribute ideas for how data and analytics can create competitive advantage across PartsSource's business.

What You'll Bring

Your Background

Bachelor's degree in data science, mathematics, economics, business, engineering, or a related quantitative field.
2–4 years of experience in data analysis, business analysis, financial analysis, or similar analytical roles.
Proficiency with SQL for data extraction and query writing; demonstrated ability to work with relational databases.
Strong Excel skills including pivot tables, VLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH, data visualization, and analysis.
Ability to translate business questions into analytical approaches; comfort working with ambiguity and defining scope.
Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple analytical projects with competing priorities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to explain analytical findings clearly to non-technical audiences.
Intellectual curiosity about data, analytics, and emerging tools; self-starter who learns new methodologies independently.

Preferred

Experience with Python or R for data manipulation and statistical analysis.
Familiarity with data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI) or BI platforms.
Experience in SaaS, healthcare, or subscription/managed service business models.
Hands-on experience with AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) and understanding of how they can enhance analytical work.
Experience developing dashboards or creating repeatable analytical processes.

Who We Want to Meet

Act Like an Owner

You take responsibility for the accuracy and quality of your analyses. You validate your work, document your methodologies clearly, and follow through on analytical commitments.
Accountability & Execution, Results Driven

Accountability & Execution, Curiosity & Problem Solving

Serve with Purpose

You understand that your analysis supports business decisions that impact PartsSource's customers and strategy. You bring analytical rigor and integrity to every project.
Clear & Critical Thinking, Active Listening

You communicate analytical findings clearly to non-technical audiences, translating complexity into actionable insights that resonate with business stakeholders.

Adapt to Thrive

You learn new tools, methodologies, and analytical approaches independently and apply feedback constructively to improve your work.
Learning Agility, Resilience

You're curious about how emerging tools like AI can enhance your analytical processes, and you actively experiment with new approaches to improve efficiency and insight quality.
Learning Agility, Innovation

Team Orientation, Alignment & Cohesion

You document your work and share knowledge with teammates, creating repeatable processes that amplify the team's impact.
Collaboration, Continuous Improvement

Challenge the Status Quo

You notice when analytical processes are inefficient and bring ideas for how to streamline workflows, reduce manual work, or improve consistency across analyses.
Curiosity & Problem Solving, Continuous Improvement

You ask why certain questions matter to the business and propose new analytical approaches that create value.
Initiative, Critical Thinking

Benefits & Perks

Lazard is one of the world’s preeminent financial advisory and asset management firms. Our people and culture make the difference
. While global in presence and reach, ours is a close, collaborativecommunity of just over 3,000 professionals. Lazard is a place of continuous knowledge sharing, skill development and relationship building, where professionals grow and succeed together. Our entrepreneurial culture, flat structure and embrace of individual differences, allow creative ideas, original concepts, and unique perspectives to drive our business forward — and for careers to take flight.

The purpose of our asset management business is to help our clients invest for the future — whether it’s for retirement, to grow and preserve inter-generational wealth, or to benefit the organizations that make our world smarter, healthier and more sustainable.

Lazard Asset Management is hiring an experienced US Healthcare Equity Research Analyst.

Backed by a 175-year heritage of independent, research-driven investing, Lazard offers analysts a rare combination: the resources and global reach of a scaled platform with the intellectual latitude and collaborative culture of a boutique. For researchers who want their ideas to matter at scale — and to help shape a platform building its next chapter of growth — there has never been a more compelling moment to build a career here.

We’ll Trust You To

Own the sector. Build and maintain a differentiated view on US pharma and biotech, including pipeline economics, patent cliffs and LOE exposure, launch trajectories, pricing and reimbursement policy, and M&A/BD capital allocation.
Generate investable ideas. Source, underwrite, and defend long ideas with a multi-year horizon, framing the durability of growth, returns on invested capital, and the gap between market expectations and your own.
Debate rigorously. Engage PMs and fellow analysts directly — pressure-test your thesis, challenge theirs, and update views as evidence changes. Intellectual honesty on what you got wrong matters as much as conviction on what you got right.
Monitor positions actively. Track catalysts (clinical readouts, FDA actions, policy shifts, earnings) and communicate thesis-changing developments quickly and unambiguously.
Maintain an expert network. Develop relationships with management teams, KOLs, physicians, payers, regulatory and policy experts, and industry consultants to source information ahead of consensus.
Advance the toolkit. Apply AI and modern research tooling to accelerate information synthesis and expand coverage depth, freeing more time for high-value judgment and portfolio construction.
Contribute to the platform. Share frameworks and sector read-throughs that make adjacent analysts and PMs better.

You’ll Need To Have

10+ years research experience covering pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, or broader healthcare,
5 or more years of track record committing capital on the buy side.
Genuine command of drug development and commercialization — clinical trial design and endpoints, FDA pathways, IP and exclusivity, and US payer and pricing dynamics.
Strong fundamental modeling and valuation skills, including DCF, sum-of-the-parts/asset-level valuation, and scenario analysis.
A long-only, quality investing orientation: focused on business durability, competitive moats, financial productivity, and multi-year compounding rather than short-term trading.
Evidence of an idea-generation track record you can walk through — theses, outcomes, and lessons from the misses.
Clear, concise written and verbal communication; able to state a thesis, the variant view, and the risk in a few sentences.
Bachelor's degree in life sciences, finance, economics, or a related field.

Preferred

Prior experience in a collaborative research platform serving multiple portfolio strategies.
Practical fluency with AI-assisted research workflows, alternative data (prescription, claims, clinical trial databases), or Python/SQL for analysis.
Advanced degree (MD, PhD, PharmD, MBA) or CFA charter.
Exposure to global healthcare beyond the US, or to medtech, life science tools, and managed care as adjacent coverage.

We strive to enhance the total health and well-being of our employees through comprehensive, competitive benefits. Our goal is to offer a highly individualized employee experience that enables you to balance your commitments to career, family, and community. When you work for Lazard, you are working for an organization that cares about your unique talents and passions, and will continue to invest in the development of your career.

Various factors contribute to determining the actual base compensation offered, including but not limited to the applicant’s years of relevant experience, career tenure, qualifications, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, relevant skills for the role. Base salary is one component of Lazard Asset Management’s compensation package, which also includes comprehensive benefits and may include incentive compensation.

Does this sound like you?

Apply! We’ll get in touch on the next steps.

Representation at Lazard

Lazard is an intellectual capital business committed to delivering the best advice and solutions to clients. To achieve these objectives, we focus on attracting, developing and retaining the best talent. We believe that a workforce comprised of people who represent a wide array of backgrounds, experiences and perspectives creates a rich variety of thought that empowers us to challenge conventional wisdom, solve problems creatively and make better decisions.

jobs.title: Scientific Project Manager (Biomedical Data Coordination)
jobs.description:
We believe that by equipping researchers with rapid insights and providers with tailored, on-demand data, we can help people lead better, healthier lives. At Digital Infuzion, we harness innovative healthcare solutions and cutting-edge bioinformatics to make meaningful impacts in patient care.

Our team thrives in a creative, open, and growth-oriented environment, guided by our core values:

Outcomes First:
Focusing on what matters most and making timely, informed decisions.

Innovative:
Embracing creativity and continuous improvement to drive novel solutions.

Radical Candor:
Communicating openly and honestly, balancing direct feedback with genuine care.

Never Satisfied:
Pursuing excellence and continuous growth beyond the status quo.

Resilient:
Adapting and persevering through challenges, turning obstacles into opportunities.

If you're passionate about leveraging technology to improve healthcare and want to work in an environment that values innovation and collaboration, we may have just the opportunity for you.

Position Overview

Digital Infuzion delivers Data Coordination Services to large multi-center research networks through a comprehensive scientific data management, sharing, and analysis platform. We are looking for an exceptional individual to serve as the Scientific Project Manager for a Data Coordination Services program supporting the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases. 

In this role, you will provide scientific and operational coordination for a multidisciplinary team supporting a mission-driven NIH program focused on infectious disease, vaccine development, translational research, and related scientific initiatives. The role will bring together expertise in biomedical research, data management, informatics, data quality, and scientific communications. Serving as a key liaison among program leadership, government stakeholders, investigators, data managers, and technical teams, the Coordinator will help ensure that scientific priorities and stakeholder needs are clearly understood and addressed. This individual will translate those priorities into coordinated activities, effective data management strategies, well-defined technical requirements, and high-quality program deliverables. 

Who You Are

The ideal candidate is a scientifically trained professional with experience coordinating complex biomedical, public health, clinical, translational, or research-focused programs.  
You are a natural organizer, task manager, and action-oriented problem solver. 
You have a desire to apply your scientific or research background to support programs that enable biomedical discovery and public health impact. 
You are comfortable working with scientists, data analysts, informatics professionals, communications specialists, technical teams, and government stakeholders. 
You are skilled at facilitating discussions, identifying areas of agreement, resolving ambiguity, and translating stakeholder needs into clear requirements and next steps. 
You have a strong sense of quality and can help teams maintain clear processes, documentation, timelines, and expectations. 
You are interested in scientific data sharing, research coordination, and the role of data quality in advancing translational and pre-clinical research. 
You are collaborative, adaptable, and able to operate effectively in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. 

Responsibilities 

Serve as a primary scientific and programmatic liaison among government stakeholders, investigators, data managers, partner organizations, and internal scientific and technical teams. 
Support the Principal Investigator and Program Manager in coordinating project activities, timelines, deliverables, priorities, risks, dependencies, and action items across scientific, data quality, communications, and technical workstreams. 
Lead or facilitate recurring meetings, scientific working groups, requirements-gathering sessions, and stakeholder discussions, documenting decisions, action items, and follow-up activities. 
Coordinate the development, implementation, and maintenance of data standards, metadata models, and data management approaches for exploratory, preclinical, translational, and related biomedical research data. 
Develop and promote data management, access, and sharing practices consistent with FAIR data principles, NIH expectations, and applicable public repository requirements. 
Translate scientific priorities and user needs into clear requirements and recommendations for data quality, informatics, software development, analytics, and AI-enabled tools. 
Coordinate technical assistance and collaboration between scientific subject matter experts and technical teams to support investigators, data managers, and other members of the program’s user community. 
Support scientific communications, outreach, and program activities, including annual meetings, conferences, webinars, presentations, websites, and stakeholder-facing materials. 
Coordinate with data quality and scientific staff to help track data submission review activities, recurring issues, process improvement opportunities, and related documentation needs. 
Draft and review contract status reports, progress updates, meeting summaries, and other program deliverables that communicate project status, accomplishments, and upcoming priorities. 

Requirements 

Master’s degree in a life science, biomedical science, or related scientific discipline; equivalent experience may be considered. 
Background supporting biomedical, translational, infectious disease, vaccine, preclinical research, or scientific data-focused programs. 
Proven ability to facilitate scientific meetings, working groups, requirements-gathering sessions, and stakeholder discussions. 
Working knowledge of scientific research workflows, research documentation, data quality concepts, and biomedical or public health data environments. 
Ability to translate scientific needs into data standards, data management processes, technical requirements, or program recommendations. 
Demonstrated success coordinating complex projects, tracking action items and deliverables, maintaining documentation, and collaborating across scientific, technical, analytical, communications, and project management teams.  
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to summarize information clearly and professionally for different audiences. 
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. 

Preferred Qualifications 

PhD in a life or biomedical science discipline, particularly biology, microbiology, immunology, virology, infectious disease research, or a related field. 
Prior work with NIH, HHS, NIAID, or another federal health agency. 
Background supporting a Data Coordinating Center or a large multi-center scientific research consortium. 
Advanced subject-matter knowledge in infectious disease, immunology, virology, vaccine development, translational science, or pre-clinical research. 
Familiarity with biomedical data standards, data quality processes, research data management, FAIR data principles, and NIH data sharing expectations. 
Experience coordinating scientific communications, outreach activities, conferences, or stakeholder engagement efforts. 
Ability to provide scientific requirements or subject matter guidance for informatics, software, analytics, AI, or machine-learning initiatives. 
Understanding of Agile practices within a software development or data management environment.

jobs.title: Partnerships & Business Operations Manager
jobs.description:
About Wolf Games

Wolf Games builds daily games for companies that already own an audience. Streamers, publishers, brands. They bring the IP and we turn it into a library of games that lives on their platform, art directed to their brand, hosted and run by us, new every day.

Every game runs a daily narrative shaped by our writers. Underneath it, a generative data loop that makes the play sharper the longer it runs.

We're early and we move fast. Game design, storytelling, and AI in one room. Small wins that lead to big wins, respect for the craft, and persistence when it gets hard.

We're not chasing hits. We're building the thing people open on a Tuesday.

About the role

Wolf is looking for a Partnerships & Business Operations Manager
to help turn important partnerships and company initiatives into products and experiences people can actually play.

Signing a partnership is only the beginning. Teams need to align, decisions need to get made, assets and approvals need to arrive, and product, engineering, creative, commercial, and partner work all need to stay connected. Your job is to help make that happen.

You’ll work directly with Wolf’s founders and across Partnerships, Product, Engineering, Creative, Marketing, Legal, and external partner teams. You’ll help create structure around ambiguous work, turn conversations into action, and make sure important details don’t fall through the cracks.

You’ll sit close to the center of the business, seeing firsthand how partnerships become products and how product, technology, creative, commercial, and audience strategy come together. Some days that means thinking through a new opportunity; others, it means tracking down a missing asset or decision blocking a launch.

Wolf is still early, and the partnerships, products, and ways we operate are being built today. You’ll start with defined pieces of important initiatives and take on increasingly meaningful ownership as you demonstrate judgment, reliability, and follow-through.

What You’ll Do

Turn Partnerships Into Products

Help move partnerships from agreement or idea through development, launch, and expansion.
Turn partner conversations and commitments into clear owners, actions, and next steps.
Keep track of deliverables, assets, approvals, timelines, and dependencies across Wolf and partner teams.
Prepare for partner meetings, capture decisions, and make sure follow-ups happen.
Build strong relationships with partner teams and grow into a trusted day-to-day counterpart.

Drive Cross-Functional Execution

Help build and manage plans for partner initiatives, products, and launches.
Coordinate across Product, Engineering, Creative, Marketing, and external teams.
Keep owners, milestones, decisions, and dependencies organized and visible.
Notice when something is blocked, unclear, or falling behind and help get it resolved.
Make sure decisions turn into action and that important details don’t fall through the cracks.
Adapt as priorities, requirements, and timelines change.

Learn What Works

Help define what success looks like for launches and partner initiatives.
Gather performance data, partner feedback, and lessons from what we ship.
Help the team understand what worked, what didn’t, and what we should do differently next time.
Carry lessons from one partnership or launch into the next.
Help identify opportunities to grow successful partnerships.

Help Build the Machine

Notice recurring problems, inefficiencies, and places where ownership is unclear.
Help create simple playbooks, workflows, templates, and tools that make execution easier.
Improve how Wolf keeps track of commitments, decisions, and next steps.
Make the team more organized and effective without adding unnecessary processes.
Take on increasingly ambiguous and important projects as you learn the business and earn trust.

What Success Looks Like

90 days in:

A strong understanding of Wolf’s partnerships, products, teams, and how work moves from idea to launch.
Partner initiatives where you’ve kept deliverables, decisions, and owners organized and moving.
Internal and external relationships where people increasingly trust you to follow through and get the right people aligned.

6 months in:

A partner initiative or launch where you’ve independently driven meaningful pieces of the work from planning through execution.
A complex project where you identified a blocker, dependency, or missing decision early and helped resolve it.
A process, tool, or workflow you’ve improved to make partnership execution more effective.

By the end of your first year:

A major partner product or initiative you helped take from idea to launch.
A partner relationship where you’ve become a trusted operating counterpart and helped identify opportunities for continued growth.
Lessons, processes, or playbooks from your work that have materially improved how Wolf executes future partnerships and launches.

The ultimate measure is simple: Wolf should be able to take on more ambitious work with more partners because you’re part of the team.

Who We’re Looking For

We care more about how you think, work, and learn than about a specific career path.

You’re likely to thrive here if:
You are exceptionally organized.
You keep track of details, commitments, and deadlines, and rarely let things fall through the cracks.
You learn quickly.
You’re curious, ask good questions, and can get up to speed on unfamiliar products, technologies, and business problems.
You’re great with people.
You communicate clearly, build relationships easily, and are comfortable working with different personalities and functions.
You turn ambiguity into action.
When something isn’t clearly defined, your instinct is to figure out what’s needed and what should happen next.
You follow through.
If you say you’ll do something, people can trust that it will get done.
You’re a clear communicator.
You can listen to a complicated conversation and pull out the important decisions, questions, and next steps.
You notice things.
Missing information, unclear ownership, potential problems, and loose ends tend to stand out to you.
You have good judgment—and want to develop more of it.
You’re comfortable making progress independently but know when to ask questions or pull someone in.
You’re willing to do whatever the work requires.
You’re as comfortable thinking through a bigger problem as you are tracking down a missing asset or following up on an overdue decision.
You want responsibility.
You’re early in your career and excited by the opportunity to learn quickly, prove yourself, and earn increasingly significant ownership.

This could be a great role for someone with roughly 2-5 years of experience
, but we care more about capability, trajectory, and demonstrated ownership
than tenure.

Relevant backgrounds might include:
Business or startup operations
Strategy & operations
Partnerships
Program or project management
Product operations
Consulting
Implementation or solutions
Media, entertainment, gaming, or technology

We’re especially interested in people who have taken ownership of something and made it happen
—whether that means shipping a cross-functional project, coordinating internal and external stakeholders, building a useful process or system, or becoming the person a team relied on to keep complicated work moving.

Compensation:
$35-45/hour, depending on experience

This role starts as a 90-day contract, at which point we can assess mutual fit and discuss conversion to a full-time role with benefits.

About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

About The Role

Join Peraton in advancing the safety, efficiency, and modernization of the National Airspace System (NAS) through the FAA's Brand New Air Traffic Control System (BNATCS) contract. As a trusted partner to the Federal Aviation Administration, Peraton helps deliver the systems and services that keep our nation's skies safe and connected. We're looking for innovative professionals who thrive in mission-critical environments and are passionate about shaping the future of air traffic management. This is your chance to make an impact on one of the world's most vital transportation infrastructures, working alongside leaders in aviation, engineering, data science, and systems integration.

At Peraton, you won't just support the mission you'll define it. Lead the work that keeps America flying safely.

At Peraton, we don't just manage projects-we deliver the systems that protect and advance U.S. air travel. We are seeking a Technical Project Manager - Senior
to lead complex, high-visibility engineering and technology initiatives supporting the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). This role sits at the heart of aviation modernization, where disciplined execution, technical excellence, and mission impact converge. If you thrive in environments where precision matters, collaboration is essential, and your work has national significance, this role offers both challenge and purpose.

Work Location:

This position is required to be on-site, primarily located in Herndon, VA, with an alternate work location available in Bowie, MD. Candidates must be able to work on-site at one of these locations based on program requirements.

In this position, you will:

Program Execution

Own the full lifecycle of sophisticated network, infrastructure, and software projects-from concept through deployment.
Translate complex engineering requirements into executable plans, schedules, and budgets using Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid methodologies.
Align technical delivery with long-term FAA modernization goals and program priorities.
Support requirements analysis, system testing, readiness reviews, and operational transitions.
Champion continuous improvement, bringing structure, consistency, and efficiency to complex engineering efforts.
Drive projects to successful completion while meeting FAA standards, cost targets, and delivery commitments.

Technical Leadership & Collaboration

Lead and coordinate cross-functional teams spanning software, hardware, networking, RAN, and systems integration.
Partner closely with vendors, engineers, and program leaders to ensure seamless execution across all technical domains.
Provide clear, confident briefings and milestone updates to FAA and senior program stakeholders.

Risk Management with Real Impact

Anticipate and resolve technical risks, dependencies, and integration challenges-especially within network and infrastructure deployments.
Ensure issues are identified early and addressed decisively to protect mission outcomes.

Trusted Stakeholder Partner

Serve as the primary bridge between technical teams, program management, and FAA leadership.
Maintain transparent communication and strong relationships that enable informed decisions and sustained confidence.

Why You'll Want This Role:

Few roles offer the opportunity to apply deep technical and project management expertise at a scale that truly matters. In this position, your leadership directly supports aviation safety, cybersecurity, and infrastructure modernization across the National Airspace System.

Your work will:

Influence systems relied upon by millions of travelers every day
Support FAA initiatives that enhance safety, capacity, and resilience
Place you at the center of high-profile, mission-critical programs

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

U.S. Citizenship Required.
Must have the ability to obtain / maintain a Public Trust clearance.
10 years of relevant experience
Demonstrated success managing technical, engineering, or IT infrastructure projects.
Hands-on Network Engineering, Cybersecurity or Software Testing experience.
Strong understanding of project management principles, risk management, and performance tracking.
Proven ability to manage project scope, schedules, budgets, risks, and dependencies using structured project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid).
Strong stakeholder management skills, with experience briefing senior leadership and external customers.
Hands-on experience with risk identification, mitigation, and issue resolution in technical project environments.
Proven ability to develop and manage detailed project schedules and budgets.
Ability to conduct technical reviews, validation activities, and post-implementation assessments.

Preferred Qualifications:

Exposure to FAA programs or NAS systems.
Experience supporting FAA NextGen, air traffic management systems, or federal technology modernization efforts.
Degree in Engineering Management, Business Administration (MBA), or Systems Engineering.
PMP (Project Management Professional) or PMI-ACP certification.
Professional certifications such as CSEP (Certified Systems Engineering Professional) or ITIL Foundations.
Background working in high-availability, safety-critical, or regulated environments (e.g., aviation, defense, transportation, or critical infrastructure).
Strong analytical and decision-making skills with a track record of delivering complex projects on time and within budget.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Technical Enablement

Scale AI’s customer-facing engineering organization is one of the fastest-growing and most technically demanding in enterprise AI. Frontier Agentic Engineers sit at the center of our most strategic relationships; building, integrating, and troubleshooting directly with customers. Until now, there has been no dedicated enablement function to support them.

As Program Manager, Technical Enablement, you will build that function from the ground up. Your job is to make sure every engineer who joins this team ramps quickly and confidently, has access to an authoritative, maintained knowledge base they can actually trust, and stays sharp as Scale’s platform and product surface evolves. You will own the full enablement lifecycle for customer-facing engineering, from day one onboarding through ongoing development, and you will be measured on ramp speed, knowledge base health, and the sustained readiness of the teams you support.

This role sits within the Enablement org and partners closely with FAE leadership, the broader Enablement team, and cross-functional stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Sales, and Delivery.

You will:

Build and Own Engineering Onboarding

Design and launch a structured, role-based onboarding program for new FAE hires, taking engineers from environment setup through meaningful technical contribution within their first 30 days.
Define fully ramped success criteria by role and communicate them clearly to new hires and their managers.

Own and Govern the Engineering Knowledge Base

Audit, consolidate, and maintain the authoritative technical knowledge base for customer-facing engineering, eliminating fragmentation, broken link chains, and stale documentation.
Establish a review cadence to keep content current as the platform evolves; tag owners and set expiration dates for key docs.
Create a clear document hierarchy so engineers always know which resources are canonical and which are deprecated.
Work with internal experts to surface the right documentation for the right audience, distinguishing what a new hire needs on Day 1 from what an established engineer needs to go deep.

Drive Ongoing Technical Development (Everboarding)

Develop and maintain a recurring enablement cadence (live sessions, async updates, release summaries) that keeps tenured engineers up to date on new capabilities, product changes, and evolving enterprise use cases.
Identify readiness gaps through feedback loops with managers and new hires, and develop targeted content to close them.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Program Management

Serve as the embedded enablement partner to FAE leadership, maintaining a close pulse on what the teams need as the business scales.
Collaborate with the broader Enablement team to adapt existing GTM enablement content for engineering audiences and bring engineering learnings back to the org.
Manage multiple concurrent programs with clear milestones, keeping stakeholders informed on roadmap progress and program effectiveness.
Report on program health and outcomes to engineering and Enablement leadership on an ongoing basis.

Ideally you’ll have:

4+ years of professional experience in enablement, program management, technical training, or a closely related role.
2+ years of program management experience, with a track record of taking programs from zero to launched in a fast-moving environment.
Experience supporting technical teams, engineers, solutions engineers, or similar, at a B2B technology company.
Strong instincts for knowledge management: you’ve built or significantly improved a documentation system and have clear opinions on what makes them work.
Comfort navigating technical content: you don’t need to write code, but you can read a technical architecture doc, identify what’s outdated, and work with engineers to fix it.
Excellent written communication skills and a bias toward creating content that people actually use.
Proficiency with AI tools for content creation, summarization, and workflow automation.

Nice to haves:

Background in developer tools, AI/ML platforms, or technical product environments where the end user is an engineer or technical practitioner.
Experience building LMS-based learning paths or structured onboarding curricula for technical audiences.
Familiarity with tiered instructional design or adult learning principles applied to technical content.
Prior experience collaborating with Product, Engineering, or Delivery teams to extract and systematize institutional knowledge.
Experience in a high-growth, venture-backed environment where you’ve built programs from scratch without waiting for perfect infrastructure.

At Scale, we are driving the future of AI and Machine Learning across a variety of industries. As the Program Manager for Compliance, you will play a pivotal role in the continued success of Scale. Your role will be instrumental in ensuring the effective operation of our Compliance department and our GRC function, allowing us to maintain the highest standards in our industry.

Reporting to the Director & Associate General Counsel, Compliance, you will be a dedicated program manager for Scale's enterprise compliance program and the person who turns policy into practice across anti-bribery and anti-corruption, gifts and entertainment, conflicts of interest, third-party risk and sanctions, policy lifecycle, and company-wide training. This is a hands-on builder, not a maintenance role.

You will support Commercial, Public Sector, and international business lines, working closely with Legal, Procurement, Finance, Security, and go-to-market teams.

You will:

Help build, design, improve, and streamline Scale's core compliance programs, including anti-bribery and anti-corruption (ABAC), gifts and entertainment, conflicts of interest, and third-party risk and sanctions screening.
Collaborate with stakeholders across the company to improve compliance policies, processes, and procedures.
Monitor regulatory developments relevant to Scale's business, translate them into concrete policy and process changes, and track compliance obligations flowing out of customer contracts.
Partner with leadership to build, mature, and operationalize the company's enterprise risk management (ERM) framework, identifying and assessing key business risks.
Build the reporting layer: metrics and periodic reporting that give Legal & GRC leadership a defensible picture of program health.
Flex into audit and assurance work during peak certification periods, and own inbound customer and investor compliance diligence questionnaires.

Ideally you'd have:

5+ years building or operating ethics and compliance programs in-house, with hands-on ownership of ABAC and at least one of gifts and entertainment, conflicts of interest, or third-party risk.
A track record of building policies, processes, and controls from scratch and successfully implementing them within a business.
Experience leading day-to-day activities and improving processes.
An action-oriented mindset, balancing creative problem-solving with a strong drive to achieve outcomes.
Strong analytical skills, with experience using data analysis tools or software.
Experience in project management, including planning, organizing, and managing resources.

Nice to haves:

Familiarity with various compliance frameworks, both auditing and implementing, such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, and NIST 800-53.
Experience applying AI or Machine Learning.
International compliance experience, particularly government contracting or public sector business in the GCC, EMEA, or APAC.
Experience with GRC tooling or third-party risk management systems, and certification such as CCEP or CCEP-I.
Current or past U.S. Government Security Clearance.

new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Us

Founded in Montreal in 2018, nesto is a Canadian fintech company on a mission to make property financing positive, empowering, and transparent from start to finish. We began as a digital mortgage broker and became Canada's leading direct-to-consumer online lending platform. Through Nesto Cloud, our B2B, cloud-native, end-to-end mortgage technology platform, we empower financial institutions, credit unions, and commercial real estate lenders with intelligent automation, real-time compliance, and seamless integrations across the full lending lifecycle. Together with CMLS Financial, we form the Nesto Group: more than $73 billion CAD in residential and commercial mortgages under management, 1,300+ team members, 12 offices across Canada.

Why We Are Hiring

As we partner with more financial institutions to modernize their mortgage operations through Nesto Cloud, we are adding two new Project Manager roles, growing our team from four to six. As Canada's most advanced cloud-based mortgage technology, our SaaS solution offers a best-in-class omnichannel experience. This platform consistently drives volume, boosts productivity, and lowers technology costs.

Work Location and Language Requirements

We are looking for one candidate in Quebec and one in Ontario, with a preference for those based in the Greater Montreal Area or Greater Toronto Area. French language proficiency is only required for the Quebec-based role.

What Success Looks Like

As a Project Manager on nesto's B2B delivery team, you'll lead large, multi-stream SaaS implementation programs for our financial-institution partners. This role combines discovery and implementation ownership, from early requirements through delivery, testing, and post-launch stabilization. You'll partner closely with product, engineering, operations, and leadership to ensure programs are delivered efficiently and all stakeholders remain aligned. In order to be successful:

You take immediate ownership and drive progress from day one, even when faced with ambiguity.
You proactively organize work and bring structure where processes don't exist.
You will identify and help implement foundational product management standards and practices – as the team was established recently, we are still building the infrastructure required for a highly efficient PM organization.
You ramp up quickly on our SaaS delivery model – enterprise SaaS delivery experience is a must.
You demonstrate strong learning agility by absorbing large amounts of new information quickly.

What You’ll Be Doing

Own the end-to-end delivery of enterprise client implementations, from discovery through deployment and post-launch transition.
Facilitate discovery workshops along side our SMEs and requirements sessions to define scope, dependencies, and timelines.
Translate business and technical requirements into actionable delivery plans using tools such as Jira and Confluence.
Coordinate with internal teams (Product, Engineering, QA, Operations) and external vendors to drive progress and resolve blockers.
Manage project budgets, schedules, and dependencies across multiple workstreams.
Provide clear, consistent communication to client and internal stakeholders, including weekly status reports, risk logs, and steering committee updates.
Track project health and proactively identify delivery risks, capacity constraints, and cross-program dependencies.
Partner with other PMs to align workstreams across major accounts
Contribute to the evolution of nesto’s delivery framework.

What You Bring

7+ years of experience in project management, with at least 3 years in SaaS environments.
Experience or understanding of non-functional requirements (e.g. monitoring, alerting, high availability, production / cloud operations), relevant to SaaS platforms.
Direct customer interaction experience, as you'll be responsible for driving customer meetings.
Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, confident interfacing with executives, clients, and technical teams.
Comfortable managing complex, ambiguous programs with many moving parts, and able to bring structure, communication, and predictability to cross-functional teams.
Advanced organizational skills and the ability to drive coordination across diverse teams.
Proficiency in project management tools such as Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or similar.
Knowledge of Agile or hybrid delivery models, with the ability to adapt process to context.

Nice-to-Have

Project management credentials & methods: PMP (Project Management Professional) and Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) and/or other agile PM certifications.
A technical background, ideally in engineering or a similar adjacent domain.
Experience working with financial institutions, mortgage or lending technology, or regulated B2B environments.
Experience using AI tools (Claude, Gemini, etc.) to improve or streamline your work and workflows.

This Role Might Be for You If

You thrive in ambiguous environments and can drive clarity without a playbook.
You enjoy building structure from scratch and take pride in leaving things more organized than you found them.
You lead with a servant-leader mindset – you enable your team rather than manage from above.
You're motivated by rapid learning and get energized when there's a lot to absorb quickly.
You welcome high leadership exposure and are comfortable presenting to senior stakeholders.
You're adaptable and can shift priorities without losing momentum.

You Shouldn’t Apply If

You don't have proven experience in a SaaS environment, or lack an understanding of operations topics like monitoring, alerting, high availability, and production/cloud operations.
Your experience is strictly internal. If you've only managed back-office projects or internal tool rollouts, you'll lack the client-facing experience this role requires.
You need a predefined playbook to succeed. We're building our processes while delivering a massive initiative, so if you need established structures and "perfect" documentation to get started, you'll find our environment frustrating.
You're coming from a large, rigid corporate environment and are looking for a slow pace or clear departmental boundaries. Our PM scope will likely feel overwhelming.

Interview Process

Recruiter Screen (30 min): An intro call to learn about your background and give you a real picture of the role.
Discovery Call (30 min): A conversation with the hiring manager to dig into your experience and assess mutual fit.
Take-Home Assignment / Case Study: A chance to showcase your skills through a practical exercise relevant to the role.
Case Study Interview (45 min): A deep dive into your submission, with time to get to know some team members and ask about the role and company.
Final Interview (60 min): You'll meet with the recruiter and two additional stakeholders for a final conversation before a decision is made.
Offer Stage: Pending successful background, criminal, and reference checks, you'll receive a formal offer to join the team.

What We Offer

Comprehensive Health Coverage: Top-tier extended health, dental, and vision coverage, featuring 100% drug coverage.
Health & Wellness Spending Account: A $1,500 combined annual flex fund for things like gym memberships or extra medical needs.
Generous Paid Time Off: 4 weeks of vacation plus 8 personal floater days.
Retirement Savings: Access to a group RRSP/DPSP plan featuring competitive company-matching contributions.
Telemedicine Services: Access via Dialogue and coverage for licensed practitioner services.
Family Support: Robust Maternity and Parental Leave Top-Up programs.

Why Join Us

The mortgage industry runs on legacy systems, slow processes, and information nobody can see. We are changing that by building better technology. nesto is a place for builders, problem-solvers, and curious minds – people who move fast, embrace innovation, and believe we're stronger together. This is the place for you if you trust your skills and want to build technology that reshapes an entire industry. An entrepreneurial culture built on trust, speed, uncomfortable ambition, being stronger together, and a relentless obsession with our clients. We also do not think building with AI belongs to engineers. Every function here is expected to automate its own repetitive work, and you will have support to do it.

Our Track Record

Hypergrowth: Deloitte Fast 50 – 3 years in a row
Tech community credibility: TechTO Canadian Rocketship 2025
Industry leadership: CLA Lending Company of the Year – 4 consecutive years
Talent magnet: CMP Top Mortgage Employer 2025

Diversity and Inclusion

At nesto, we believe that creativity and collaboration are the result of a diverse team. We are committed to fostering a culture of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging, and we strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and individuals with disabilities to apply. We are committed to creating a workplace that is inclusive and welcoming to all.

new_jobs.title: Enterprise Systems Program Delivery Manager
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Enterprise Systems Program Delivery Manager

(Remote)

About Us

Matrix Medical Network is the nation’s leading independent provider of comprehensive in-home health assessments, serving Medicare Advantage, Managed Medicaid and Commercial patients across all 50 states. With a network of 3,000 + clinicians, we deliver personalized Whole Person Care that includes diagnostic testing, risk identification, medication management and preventive health education, empowering people to better manage acute and chronic conditions. Guided by our mantra- We see you. We hear you. We’ve got you. - and our core values of Integrity, Accountability, Trust, Respect and Passion, we are committed to creating a culture where both patients and teammates feel valued, supported and heard.

Why Work at Matrix?

The opportunity to work with one of the fastest growing companies in healthcare whose vision is to provide unparalleled quality and value to providers and members.
A chance to work with great people on exciting projects.
Our opportunities allow you to leverage your expertise and compassion, making a direct impact to the health and well-being of members.
Competitive Compensation: Be rewarded for your effort and passion while making a difference in the community.

Responsibilities

About the Role

Type: Full-Time, Salaried
Compensation: $134,000 - $202,000, 20% incentive bonus
Location: Fully Remote (must be located in the United States)
Hours: Full-Time, Days
Benefits Offered: Medical, dental, vision, paid time off, paid holidays, 401(k) with company matching, voluntary life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, employee assistance program, health savings account, flexible spending accounts, and additional voluntary benefits.

Position Summary

The Manager, Enterprise Systems & Program Delivery is a hands-on project and program leadership role responsible for driving the execution of enterprise technology initiatives that support key business functions. This role independently owns and delivers projects end to end as a strong collaborator, while also supporting the Director on larger, more complex, cross-functional initiatives by managing workstreams, coordinating dependencies, and maintaining delivery rigor.

The ideal candidate brings solid project management fundamentals, strong organizational and communication skills, and a working knowledge of enterprise systems and integrations. They will manage day-to-day execution, track and report on progress, and serve as a reliable partner to business and technical stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle — from planning through implementation and post-go-live support.

Key Responsibilities

Project & Program Delivery

Independently plan, manage, and deliver enterprise systems projects from initiation through close, ensuring on-time, in-scope delivery.
Support the Director on larger, more complex initiatives by owning defined workstreams, deliverables, or project phases.

Prime Data Centers develops, acquires, and operates data centers for some of the world's largest enterprises. Enable D&E leaders to scale by owning the planning, coordination, and execution mechanics of a growing project portfolio — so the team spends its time leading and building, not chasing status.

D&E is a small, high-leverage team carrying a workload that outpaces its headcount. This is a high-impact Individual Contributor (IC) role with broad visibility across Design, Engineering, Construction, Procurement, and Operations — not a project-coordination or administrative seat. You'll have real influence over how D&E plans, tracks, and delivers, how D&E develops and designs for the future, and real accountability for whether that execution is predictable.

This role is intentionally banded across “Sr.” and “Principal” levels — final leveling, title, and compensation will be calibrated to the experience and scope the selected candidate brings, not fixed in advance.

What You'll Do

PROGRAM PLANNING & EXECUTION

Establish and maintain systems to enable D&E's design, engineering, and construction workstreams.
Define milestones, success criteria, and delivery timelines; own the systems (Asana, Procore, and equivalents) that make status answerable in one lookup, not a scramble.
Track progress and surface risk, scope, and schedule tradeoffs early enough for leaders to act on them — not after they've already landed.
Progress programmatic initiatives to ensure a scalable, industry-leading D&E team into the future.

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COORDINATION

Serve as the connective tissue between D&E and Construction, Operations, Commercial, Development, Procurement, and Sustainability — driving alignment on process, priorities, and sequencing, not just reporting on them.
Facilitate decision-making forums and escalation paths; hold teams accountable to agreed plans and timelines without relying on formal authority.
Represent D&E's program status and risk posture directly to stakeholders and leadership, including in forums the VP, Design & Engineering isn't in.

METRICS, REPORTING & OPERATING RHYTHM

Define and maintain program dashboards and status reporting for D&E leadership and cross-functional partners.
Support quarterly and monthly planning cadences, including RFP/procurement tracking and Prime Engineering Standards distribution to stakeholders.
Identify and close recurring process gaps — a report nobody trusts, a handoff that keeps dropping — without being told to.
Facilitate third-party business reviews to ensure true collaborative partnerships are maintained.

Qualifications

6+ years leading technical programs or complex initiatives — construction, real estate development, infrastructure, or complex hardware/engineering environments strongly preferred.
Strong systems thinking; able to translate strategy into executable, trackable plans — and to build the tracking systems (Asana, Procore, or equivalent) that make that possible for others, not just yourself.
Confidence working across senior technical and business stakeholders — comfortable pushing back on an unrealistic date or dependency with data, not staying quiet.
Thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments — you'll be building parts of this operating rhythm from scratch, not running an existing playbook.
Data center, hyperscale, or mission-critical facilities experience is a strong plus, not a requirement.
PMP or equivalent project management certification is a strong plus, not a requirement.

Job Description:

About Altera

At Altera™, our independence as the world’s largest pure‑play FPGA solutions provider gives us the focus, speed, and agility to innovate without compromise. With more than four decades of industry‑leading FPGA expertise, our singular mission is to deliver the programmable technologies that help customers differentiate, innovate, and scale across rapidly evolving markets like AI, cloud, networking, and edge. As an independent company, we move faster, invest deeper, and partner more closely—empowering our teams to drive breakthrough innovation and shape the future of the FPGA industry.

About The Role

We are seeking a highly experienced Senior EDA Physical Design Technical Program Manager
to lead complex, high-impact technical programs across our Physical Design, EDA, CAD, and semiconductor engineering organizations. This role will operate at a senior level, partnering directly with engineering leadership, architects, software developers, physical design engineers, CAD/EDA teams, product teams, and other cross-functional stakeholders to drive execution of strategic initiatives supporting next-generation FPGA technologies and design automation solutions.

The Senior EDA TPM will have broad ownership of programs spanning multiple engineering organizations and will be responsible for driving programs from strategy and definition through execution, delivery, and operationalization
. This individual will establish program structure, define execution strategies, identify critical dependencies, manage technical and organizational risks, and ensure alignment across teams with competing priorities.

The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of technical program management leadership, semiconductor/EDA domain expertise, and demonstrated experience leading large, highly complex engineering programs
. The ability to understand technical challenges, anticipate execution risks, influence senior engineering leaders, and drive decisions without direct authority is essential.

This role requires a high degree of autonomy and leadership. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted program partner to senior engineering leadership, provide executive-level visibility into strategic programs, and proactively identify opportunities to improve organizational execution, processes, and engineering efficiency.

Responsibilities

Lead end-to-end execution of highly complex, strategic technical programs supporting EDA, Physical Design, CAD, semiconductor development, and next-generation FPGA technologies.
Own program strategy, scope, objectives, success criteria, execution plans, milestones, dependencies, and delivery commitments across multiple engineering organizations.
Partner closely with senior engineering leaders and architects to translate business and technical objectives into executable program strategies and roadmaps.

Establish and maintain integrated program plans encompassing schedules, milestones, critical paths, dependencies, resource requirements, deliverables, and risk mitigation strategies.
Identify critical technical and organizational risks early, develop mitigation strategies, and drive issues to resolution with appropriate stakeholders and leadership.
Proactively identify cross-program dependencies and potential execution conflicts, driving alignment and prioritization across engineering organizations.
Establish program operating mechanisms, including executive reviews, engineering checkpoints, milestone reviews, dashboards, metrics, escalation paths, and decision-making forums.
Develop executive-level reporting and communication that clearly articulates program health, accomplishments, risks, dependencies, resource constraints, decisions required, and recovery plans.
Present program status and recommendations to senior engineering leadership and executive stakeholders, including clear escalation of issues requiring leadership decisions.
Influence senior technical stakeholders and engineering leaders without direct authority to drive alignment, accountability, and timely execution.
Facilitate resolution of complex technical and organizational issues by bringing the appropriate stakeholders together, driving data-based decisions, and maintaining momentum toward program objectives.
Partner with engineering management to assess resource requirements, staffing constraints, technical priorities, and tradeoffs necessary to meet program commitments.
Drive prioritization and sequencing decisions across multiple engineering teams when resource or schedule constraints create competing priorities.
Develop and maintain multi-quarter and/or multi-year technical roadmaps for strategic EDA and Physical Design initiatives in partnership with engineering leadership.
Coordinate major technology transitions, methodology changes, tool deployments, infrastructure initiatives, and engineering process improvements across distributed organizations.
Apply strong understanding of semiconductor development and Physical Design methodologies to identify technical dependencies, anticipate execution challenges, and effectively communicate with engineering teams.
Drive programs involving EDA tool flows, design methodologies, physical implementation, timing closure, design automation, infrastructure, and engineering productivity.
Establish program-level metrics and operational mechanisms to measure execution effectiveness, identify trends, and improve predictability.
Drive continuous improvement of program management practices, engineering processes, and organizational operating mechanisms.
Identify systemic execution challenges and develop scalable solutions that improve engineering productivity, quality, predictability, and time-to-market.
Lead cross-functional retrospectives and ensure lessons learned are translated into measurable process improvements.
Mentor and provide guidance to other Technical Program Managers and project leads, helping establish consistent program management practices across the organization.
Foster a culture of accountability, transparency, proactive risk management, and cross-functional collaboration across geographically distributed engineering teams.
Operate effectively in an environment where requirements, priorities, technologies, and organizational structures may evolve rapidly.

The pay range below is for Bay Area California only. Actual salary may vary based on a number of factors including job location, job-related knowledge, skills, experiences, trainings, etc. We also offer incentive opportunities that reward employees based on individual and company performance.

new_jobs.description:
Bering-Alaka`ina Holdings, LLC is looking for an Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM)
for our customer located at Creech AFB in Indian Springs, Nevada
.

The ISSM provides dedicated strategic cybersecurity leadership and oversight for designated classified information system enclaves supporting the 25th Attack Group (25 ATKW). Unlike a hybrid or tactical operations role, this position focuses exclusively on system-level cybersecurity governance, Risk Management Framework (RMF) compliance, and continuous monitoring to achieve and maintain Authorizations to Operate (ATO). The ISSM serves as the primary cybersecurity technical advisor to the Government Authorizing Official (AO), Program Manager (PM), and Information System Owner (ISO).

DESCRIPTION OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

Serve as the formally appointed Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM) for up to four contractor managed Information Systems (including RPA Low, ACN, Audio MLS, and RPA High), overseeing the full lifecycle of cybersecurity compliance and system accreditation in accordance with DoDI 8510.01, AFI 17 101 (RMF), and AFMAN 17-1301 (COMPUSEC).
Develop, maintain, and oversee authorization documentation, System Security Plans (SSPs), risk assessments, and continuous monitoring activities using both eMASS and Xacta workflow platforms.
Act as the primary interface with Government Authorizing Officials (AOs) and Security Control Assessors (SCAs) to present risk assessments, initiate ATO packages, manage Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), and secure timely renewals.
Maintain rigorous oversight of vulnerability management, incident reporting, access control governance, and configuration management functions across assigned enclaves.
Provide oversight and guidance to subordinate cybersecurity personnel (ISSOs) to ensure security control implementation and mitigation efforts align with established baselines and mission requirements.
Provide contingency continuity support for tactical enclave cybersecurity (ISSO) activities during periods of workforce shortfalls or as critical mission needs dictate.
Report conditions that materially affect system authorization status or cybersecurity posture directly to the Government, translating technical risk into actionable mission risk.
Initiate exceptions, deviations, or waivers to cybersecurity requirements when operational impacts dictate, ensuring complete documentation and coordination with the AO.
Ensure all assigned personnel and systems remain compliant with applicable DoW/DoD 8140 cybersecurity workforce requirements.
Perform all other position related duties, as assigned, or requested.

Work Environment, Physical and Mental Demands:
Typical office environment with no unusual hazards, occasional lifting of 20 pounds, kneeling, standing, and walking, routinely sitting and constant use of speech/hearing abilities for communication, constant mental alertness, and must be able to work under deadlines

REQUIRED DEGREE/EDUCATION/CERTIFICATION:

A BS degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Information Systems, Computer Science, or equivalently relative discipline, from an ABET accredited or CAE designated institution.
Active DoD 8140 / DoDI 8570.01-M IAM Level II or III Certification matched to ISSM responsibilities prior to hiring
Must possess and maintain a valid state-issued driver’s license.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Minimum three to five (3-5) years of dedicated experience in RMF package development, continuous monitoring, and acting as an ISSM or lead ISSO.
Demonstrated proficiency in navigating and managing ATO packages within both eMASS and Xacta. Experience with STIGs, SCAP, vulnerability scanning, and ACAS/NESSUS.
Knowledge of cybersecurity laws, regulations, policies, governance, and technical safeguards governing the use, processing, storage, and transmission of classified information.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to confidently brief senior government leadership (AOs, SCAs, PMs) on cyber risk posture.

DESIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Master’s degree in a Cybersecurity or related field.
Experience with COMSEC accounts.
Understanding of GSA approved security containers and locks.

REQUIRED CITIZENSHIP AND CLEARANCE:

U.S. Citizenship is required.
Active Top Secret Clearance with the ability to obtain and maintain SCI access.

The company is looking for a business operations manager to help turn a fast-moving organization into a more effective, scalable one.

This role will work across the business on the operating rhythms, planning processes, and cross-functional coordination that help teams move faster with better judgment. That means building clarity where things are messy, creating structure where structure is missing, and helping leadership make decisions with a stronger grasp of tradeoffs, priorities, and execution risk.

On any given week, this individual might be building a planning model, improving an internal process, driving a cross-functional initiative, preparing materials for an important decision, or helping close gaps between commercial, product, infrastructure, and finance priorities.

The ideal candidate is analytical, organized, practical, and unusually strong at making things run better. They should be comfortable with ambiguity, able to earn trust across functions, and motivated by the idea of being a force multiplier for a lean, ambitious team.

In the first 8-12 months, the successful candidate will have improved the company’s operating cadence, brought more structure to planning and prioritization, made key cross-functional work easier to execute, and helped leadership spend less time chasing information and more time making good decisions.

About Glean

Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles.

At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level.

Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality.

If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more - deeply embedded where people get things done. You’ll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company.

About The Role

Glean is seeking an AI Data Analyst to help power the human evaluation system behind Glean’s AI product quality. This role sits at the centre of response quality, competitive benchmarking, and release readiness. You will evaluate AI outputs, label and categorize failure modes, maintain high-quality benchmark data, and help ensure the datasets and evals we rely on are realistic, consistent, and tied to measurable product quality lift. This is a highly cross-functional role. You will work closely with QA, Engineering, Product, and the evals team to convert ambiguous quality issues into structured data, actionable feedback, and repeatable quality signals.

You Will

Run ongoing human labeling for priority AI workflows, including response quality, task success, MCP and tool use, end-to-end Cowork-style workflows.
Triage bad-query reports, downvotes, escalations, and routed quality issues; categorize failure modes and feed clean analysis back to partner teams.
Perform qualitative analysis to identify recurring patterns such as hallucinations, retrieval failures, tool-use issues, weak grounding, and poor workflow completion.
Follow and improve labeling guidelines and rubrics so judgments are consistent, realistic, and useful for model and product improvement.
Maintain high-quality labeled datasets, golden sets, and regression slices; monitor coverage, drift, leakage, and difficulty distribution.
Participate in calibration exercises with human graders and validate LLM-as-a-judge outputs against human labels to improve consistency and judge quality.
Partner with engineers, PMs, QA, and eval owners on pre/post-change quality reads, benchmark updates, and release-readiness decisions.
Contribute to recurring quality reporting by surfacing top failure modes, coverage gaps, quality shifts, and actionable recommendations.

About You

3–5 years of experience in data labeling, data analysis, QA, or a related field.
Strong analytical judgment and attention to detail, with the ability to apply nuanced rubrics consistently.
Experience evaluating AI-generated outputs or working with NLP, search, recommendation, or other ML systems.
Familiarity with structured qualitative analysis, basic SQL/data retrieval, and spreadsheet-based workflows.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to work independently in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and collaborate effectively across functions.

Location:

This role is hybrid (4 days a week in our offices).

Compensation & Benefits

Excellent verbal briefing skills and the ability to mentor other analysts in verbal briefing.

Effective problem-solving skills.

The Data Analyst supports PartsSource's growth and operational excellence by transforming raw data into actionable insights. Working with business stakeholders across sales, operations, product, and finance, you will conduct detailed analyses on customer behavior, operational metrics, and business opportunities—identifying patterns, trends, and optimization opportunities. This role combines technical data skills with business acumen to answer complex questions, support strategic decisions, and uncover new value creation opportunities. You'll develop repeatable analytical processes, document findings clearly for diverse audiences, and stay curious about how emerging tools—including AI—can enhance analytical quality and efficiency.

Conduct detailed quantitative analyses to identify patterns, trends, and insights that address specific business questions.

Validate analytical work for accuracy and completeness; document methodologies and assumptions clearly.

Develop clear, compelling reports and dashboards that translate complex findings into actionable recommendations for business stakeholders.

Collaborate with stakeholders to understand analytical needs and define scope for data projects.

Process Improvement & Tool Development

Identify opportunities to streamline analytical workflows and reduce manual work through better processes or automation.
Create and document repeatable analysis templates, queries, and workflows that enable consistent output and knowledge sharing across the team.
Stay current with emerging analytical tools and methodologies, including practical applications of AI; experiment with new approaches to enhance efficiency and insight quality.
Support team members in understanding analytical methodologies and best practices.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Work with sales, operations, product, and finance teams to understand their analytical needs and deliver insights that support business decisions.
Translate between technical analytical concepts and business language to ensure clarity and alignment.
Contribute ideas for how data and analytics can create competitive advantage across PartsSource's business.

What You'll Bring

Your Background

Bachelor's degree in data science, mathematics, economics, business, engineering, or a related quantitative field.
2–4 years of experience in data analysis, business analysis, financial analysis, or similar analytical roles.
Proficiency with SQL for data extraction and query writing; demonstrated ability to work with relational databases.
Strong Excel skills including pivot tables, VLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH, data visualization, and analysis.
Ability to translate business questions into analytical approaches; comfort working with ambiguity and defining scope.
Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple analytical projects with competing priorities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to explain analytical findings clearly to non-technical audiences.
Intellectual curiosity about data, analytics, and emerging tools; self-starter who learns new methodologies independently.

Preferred

Experience with Python or R for data manipulation and statistical analysis.
Familiarity with data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI) or BI platforms.
Experience in SaaS, healthcare, or subscription/managed service business models.
Hands-on experience with AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) and understanding of how they can enhance analytical work.
Experience developing dashboards or creating repeatable analytical processes.

Act Like an Owner

You take responsibility for the accuracy and quality of your analyses. You validate your work, document your methodologies clearly, and follow through on analytical commitments.
Accountability & Execution, Results Driven

You communicate analytical findings clearly to non-technical audiences, translating complexity into actionable insights that resonate with business stakeholders.

Adapt to Thrive

You learn new tools, methodologies, and analytical approaches independently and apply feedback constructively to improve your work.
Learning Agility, Resilience

You're curious about how emerging tools like AI can enhance your analytical processes, and you actively experiment with new approaches to improve efficiency and insight quality.
Learning Agility, Innovation

You work effectively with cross-functional teams, asking clarifying questions to understand business needs and tailoring your analysis and communication to different audiences.
Team Orientation, Alignment & Cohesion

You document your work and share knowledge with teammates, creating repeatable processes that amplify the team's impact.
Collaboration, Continuous Improvement

Challenge the Status Quo

You notice when analytical processes are inefficient and bring ideas for how to streamline workflows, reduce manual work, or improve consistency across analyses.
Curiosity & Problem Solving, Continuous Improvement

You ask why certain questions matter to the business and propose new analytical approaches that create value.
Initiative, Critical Thinking

Career and professional development through training, coaching and new experiences.
