new_jobs.description:
RIVR, part of Amazon is a robotics company pioneering Physical AI through real-world doorstep delivery. Founded in 2024 as an ETH Zurich spin-off, RIVR developed wheeled-legged robots designed to operate in complex, unstructured environments such as stairs, gates, doors, and uneven urban terrain. We believe that achieving general physical intelligence requires solving real customer problems in the real world, where robots can learn from rich operational data at scale.

Following our acquisition by Amazon in March 2026, we are continuing this mission with greater reach and speed. By combining custom robot hardware, onboard autonomy, and cloud-based coordination, RIVR, part of Amazon is building the next generation of safe, reliable autonomous robots for last-mile delivery

Job Description

Building robots that can navigate the real world is only part of the challenge. Scaling the company behind them means connecting people, systems, locations, and decisions across Amazon RIVR and teams across Amazon.

This is a newly created role and the first at Amazon RIVR with dedicated program ownership across our portfolio of corporate initiatives. You will sit at the intersection of our engineering and operations priorities and Amazon’s global corporate functions, translating complex, undefined business objectives into structured, executable programs.

Success in this role will mean establishing the mechanisms and playbooks that connect our robotics workflows with Amazon’s corporate requirements and operating standards, while preserving the speed and ownership that have defined RIVR from day one. You will be an exceptional simplifier: someone who sees across organizational boundaries, turns overlapping requirements into clear and predictable ways of working, and makes Amazon’s infrastructure work effectively for RIVR.

What You’ll Be Doing

Own the integrated portfolio: Maintain the end-to-end roadmap for Amazon RIVR’s cross-functional corporate programs spanning Finance, Legal, People, Workplace and Real Estate, and international operations
Define and launch programs: Turn undefined business objectives into clear outcomes, scope, workstreams, owners, decision rights, milestones, and measures of success
Connect Amazon RIVR and Amazon: Bring together Amazon RIVR leaders, functional owners, and Amazon specialist teams, translating business needs and enterprise requirements into coordinated implementation plans
Establish the operating mechanisms: Build the governance, working rhythms, decision records, and implementation playbooks needed to create visibility, accountability, and momentum across workstreams
Drive decisions and alignment: Surface trade-offs, resolve conflicting priorities, and secure decisions and resource commitments from senior stakeholders across the organization
Anticipate risk and protect continuity: Identify dependencies, compliance requirements, resource constraints, and operational risks before they affect engineering, production, or operational delivery
Support our evolving international footprint: Lead cross-functional programs connected to how Amazon RIVR operates across locations, coordinating changes to processes, systems, services, and ways of working
Communicate clearly at every level: Produce concise decision documents, program reviews, and executive updates that make progress, risks, and trade-offs easy to understand

What You Must Have

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience
6+ years of experience leading complex, cross-functional programs in business operations, corporate integration, transformation, international expansion, or a comparable environment
Experience establishing a new program, operating model, or way of working where no complete playbook previously existed
A track record of taking ambiguous business objectives from initial definition through implementation and measurable delivery
Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple specialist teams and drive outcomes through influence rather than direct authority
Strong judgment and sufficient business fluency across corporate functions to engage credibly with subject-matter experts without needing to be one yourself
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience turning complex information into clear decisions and recommendations for senior leaders
Comfort moving between strategic questions and hands-on execution

Get some bonus points

Experience with post-acquisition integration or helping a growing company operate effectively within a larger organization
Experience leading programs involving corporate systems or service transitions, entity or operating-model changes, or workplace expansion
Experience working across international teams, locations, or regulatory environments
Experience supporting an engineering-led, hardware, manufacturing, or similarly complex technical organization
Strong change-management skills and experience helping teams adopt new processes or ways of working
Familiarity with Amazon’s operating mechanisms, planning processes, or corporate infrastructure

new_jobs.title: Scientific Project Manager (Biomedical Data Coordination)
new_jobs.description:
We believe that by equipping researchers with rapid insights and providers with tailored, on-demand data, we can help people lead better, healthier lives. At Digital Infuzion, we harness innovative healthcare solutions and cutting-edge bioinformatics to make meaningful impacts in patient care.

Our team thrives in a creative, open, and growth-oriented environment, guided by our core values:

Outcomes First:
Focusing on what matters most and making timely, informed decisions.

Innovative:
Embracing creativity and continuous improvement to drive novel solutions.

Radical Candor:
Communicating openly and honestly, balancing direct feedback with genuine care.

Never Satisfied:
Pursuing excellence and continuous growth beyond the status quo.

Resilient:
Adapting and persevering through challenges, turning obstacles into opportunities.

If you're passionate about leveraging technology to improve healthcare and want to work in an environment that values innovation and collaboration, we may have just the opportunity for you.

Position Overview

Digital Infuzion delivers Data Coordination Services to large multi-center research networks through a comprehensive scientific data management, sharing, and analysis platform. We are looking for an exceptional individual to serve as the Scientific Project Manager for a Data Coordination Services program supporting the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases. 

In this role, you will provide scientific and operational coordination for a multidisciplinary team supporting a mission-driven NIH program focused on infectious disease, vaccine development, translational research, and related scientific initiatives. The role will bring together expertise in biomedical research, data management, informatics, data quality, and scientific communications. Serving as a key liaison among program leadership, government stakeholders, investigators, data managers, and technical teams, the Coordinator will help ensure that scientific priorities and stakeholder needs are clearly understood and addressed. This individual will translate those priorities into coordinated activities, effective data management strategies, well-defined technical requirements, and high-quality program deliverables. 

Who You Are

The ideal candidate is a scientifically trained professional with experience coordinating complex biomedical, public health, clinical, translational, or research-focused programs.  
You are a natural organizer, task manager, and action-oriented problem solver. 
You have a desire to apply your scientific or research background to support programs that enable biomedical discovery and public health impact. 
You are comfortable working with scientists, data analysts, informatics professionals, communications specialists, technical teams, and government stakeholders. 
You are skilled at facilitating discussions, identifying areas of agreement, resolving ambiguity, and translating stakeholder needs into clear requirements and next steps. 
You have a strong sense of quality and can help teams maintain clear processes, documentation, timelines, and expectations. 
You are interested in scientific data sharing, research coordination, and the role of data quality in advancing translational and pre-clinical research. 
You are collaborative, adaptable, and able to operate effectively in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. 

Responsibilities 

Serve as a primary scientific and programmatic liaison among government stakeholders, investigators, data managers, partner organizations, and internal scientific and technical teams. 
Support the Principal Investigator and Program Manager in coordinating project activities, timelines, deliverables, priorities, risks, dependencies, and action items across scientific, data quality, communications, and technical workstreams. 
Lead or facilitate recurring meetings, scientific working groups, requirements-gathering sessions, and stakeholder discussions, documenting decisions, action items, and follow-up activities. 
Coordinate the development, implementation, and maintenance of data standards, metadata models, and data management approaches for exploratory, preclinical, translational, and related biomedical research data. 
Develop and promote data management, access, and sharing practices consistent with FAIR data principles, NIH expectations, and applicable public repository requirements. 
Translate scientific priorities and user needs into clear requirements and recommendations for data quality, informatics, software development, analytics, and AI-enabled tools. 
Coordinate technical assistance and collaboration between scientific subject matter experts and technical teams to support investigators, data managers, and other members of the program’s user community. 
Support scientific communications, outreach, and program activities, including annual meetings, conferences, webinars, presentations, websites, and stakeholder-facing materials. 
Coordinate with data quality and scientific staff to help track data submission review activities, recurring issues, process improvement opportunities, and related documentation needs. 
Draft and review contract status reports, progress updates, meeting summaries, and other program deliverables that communicate project status, accomplishments, and upcoming priorities. 

Requirements 

Master’s degree in a life science, biomedical science, or related scientific discipline; equivalent experience may be considered. 
Background supporting biomedical, translational, infectious disease, vaccine, preclinical research, or scientific data-focused programs. 
Proven ability to facilitate scientific meetings, working groups, requirements-gathering sessions, and stakeholder discussions. 
Working knowledge of scientific research workflows, research documentation, data quality concepts, and biomedical or public health data environments. 
Ability to translate scientific needs into data standards, data management processes, technical requirements, or program recommendations. 
Demonstrated success coordinating complex projects, tracking action items and deliverables, maintaining documentation, and collaborating across scientific, technical, analytical, communications, and project management teams.  
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to summarize information clearly and professionally for different audiences. 
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. 

Preferred Qualifications 

PhD in a life or biomedical science discipline, particularly biology, microbiology, immunology, virology, infectious disease research, or a related field. 
Prior work with NIH, HHS, NIAID, or another federal health agency. 
Background supporting a Data Coordinating Center or a large multi-center scientific research consortium. 
Advanced subject-matter knowledge in infectious disease, immunology, virology, vaccine development, translational science, or pre-clinical research. 
Familiarity with biomedical data standards, data quality processes, research data management, FAIR data principles, and NIH data sharing expectations. 
Experience coordinating scientific communications, outreach activities, conferences, or stakeholder engagement efforts. 
Ability to provide scientific requirements or subject matter guidance for informatics, software, analytics, AI, or machine-learning initiatives. 
Understanding of Agile practices within a software development or data management environment.

new_jobs.title: Partnerships & Business Operations Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Wolf Games

Wolf Games builds daily games for companies that already own an audience. Streamers, publishers, brands. They bring the IP and we turn it into a library of games that lives on their platform, art directed to their brand, hosted and run by us, new every day.

Every game runs a daily narrative shaped by our writers. Underneath it, a generative data loop that makes the play sharper the longer it runs.

We're early and we move fast. Game design, storytelling, and AI in one room. Small wins that lead to big wins, respect for the craft, and persistence when it gets hard.

We're not chasing hits. We're building the thing people open on a Tuesday.

About the role

Wolf is looking for a Partnerships & Business Operations Manager
to help turn important partnerships and company initiatives into products and experiences people can actually play.

Signing a partnership is only the beginning. Teams need to align, decisions need to get made, assets and approvals need to arrive, and product, engineering, creative, commercial, and partner work all need to stay connected. Your job is to help make that happen.

You’ll work directly with Wolf’s founders and across Partnerships, Product, Engineering, Creative, Marketing, Legal, and external partner teams. You’ll help create structure around ambiguous work, turn conversations into action, and make sure important details don’t fall through the cracks.

You’ll sit close to the center of the business, seeing firsthand how partnerships become products and how product, technology, creative, commercial, and audience strategy come together. Some days that means thinking through a new opportunity; others, it means tracking down a missing asset or decision blocking a launch.

Wolf is still early, and the partnerships, products, and ways we operate are being built today. You’ll start with defined pieces of important initiatives and take on increasingly meaningful ownership as you demonstrate judgment, reliability, and follow-through.

What You’ll Do

Turn Partnerships Into Products

Help move partnerships from agreement or idea through development, launch, and expansion.
Turn partner conversations and commitments into clear owners, actions, and next steps.
Keep track of deliverables, assets, approvals, timelines, and dependencies across Wolf and partner teams.
Prepare for partner meetings, capture decisions, and make sure follow-ups happen.
Build strong relationships with partner teams and grow into a trusted day-to-day counterpart.

Drive Cross-Functional Execution

Help build and manage plans for partner initiatives, products, and launches.
Coordinate across Product, Engineering, Creative, Marketing, and external teams.
Keep owners, milestones, decisions, and dependencies organized and visible.
Notice when something is blocked, unclear, or falling behind and help get it resolved.
Make sure decisions turn into action and that important details don’t fall through the cracks.
Adapt as priorities, requirements, and timelines change.

Learn What Works

Help define what success looks like for launches and partner initiatives.
Gather performance data, partner feedback, and lessons from what we ship.
Help the team understand what worked, what didn’t, and what we should do differently next time.
Carry lessons from one partnership or launch into the next.
Help identify opportunities to grow successful partnerships.

Help Build the Machine

Notice recurring problems, inefficiencies, and places where ownership is unclear.
Help create simple playbooks, workflows, templates, and tools that make execution easier.
Improve how Wolf keeps track of commitments, decisions, and next steps.
Make the team more organized and effective without adding unnecessary processes.
Take on increasingly ambiguous and important projects as you learn the business and earn trust.

What Success Looks Like

90 days in:

A strong understanding of Wolf’s partnerships, products, teams, and how work moves from idea to launch.
Partner initiatives where you’ve kept deliverables, decisions, and owners organized and moving.
Internal and external relationships where people increasingly trust you to follow through and get the right people aligned.

6 months in:

A partner initiative or launch where you’ve independently driven meaningful pieces of the work from planning through execution.
A complex project where you identified a blocker, dependency, or missing decision early and helped resolve it.
A process, tool, or workflow you’ve improved to make partnership execution more effective.

By the end of your first year:

A major partner product or initiative you helped take from idea to launch.
A partner relationship where you’ve become a trusted operating counterpart and helped identify opportunities for continued growth.
Lessons, processes, or playbooks from your work that have materially improved how Wolf executes future partnerships and launches.

The ultimate measure is simple: Wolf should be able to take on more ambitious work with more partners because you’re part of the team.

Who We’re Looking For

We care more about how you think, work, and learn than about a specific career path.

You’re likely to thrive here if:
You are exceptionally organized.
You keep track of details, commitments, and deadlines, and rarely let things fall through the cracks.
You learn quickly.

This role will also be instrumental in supporting the rollout of our new OneStream consolidation tool, partnering closely with the Financial Systems and Analytics team to help design, test, and adopt improved close and reporting processes. Strong understanding of intercompany accounting and elimination processes in a multi-entity environment

Summary:

The Creators initiative is a high-visibility program designed to identify high-potential content creators and accelerate their audience growth through dedicated, white-glove support. Operating under a venture capital model, the program identifies breakout talent, provides targeted investments to accelerate growth, and graduates established creators to onboard subsequent cohorts.

Creator Selection: Identify high-potential creators by leveraging data analytics alongside nuanced cultural and audience judgment.
Program Execution: Direct day-to-day operations and coordinate cross-functional alignment across Product, Marketing, Partnerships, and other internal teams to deliver comprehensive support.
Cohort Performance Management: Maintain detailed oversight of cohort metrics; monitor reach, distribution, and content quality to inform decisions regarding continued investment or offboarding.
Advocacy & Strategic Insights: Track and document notable instances of cross-platform creator advocacy and report key success stories to executive leadership.
Creator Experience Strategy: Refine selection messaging, communication protocols, and engagement frameworks across the full program lifecycle.
Analytical Research: Utilize performance dashboards, AI/LLM tools, and market research to monitor engagement dynamics and broader cultural trends.

Resourcefulness: A self-directed operating style with the ability to function effectively within a lean team structure and leverage emerging technologies independently.
Product Awareness: While core product infrastructure is established, basic product acumen is beneficial to complement cultural judgment and leadership capabilities.

Cultural intuition / creator judgment — a proven "nose" for spotting breakout creators who resonate across US & Canadian audiences.
Program & stakeholder management — able to run a complex, high-profile program end-to-end and drive cross-functional delivery (Marketing, Partnerships, Product, Engineering) without direct authority.
Data-informed decision-making — comfortable using dashboards, metrics, and AI/LLM tools to evaluate creators and manage cohort performance.
Creator-economy background — experience with similar programs (YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat) or media/entertainment/talent management.
